claims.value: Höpfner estimates about 40,000 French fighting 46,000 Russians after Verdier arrived at about 10 a. m.
claims.rationale: Source clock and staged fighting population; not a replacement for Bodart’s whole-day available totals. English rendering (ours): "At 10 o’clock Verdier’s division of Lannes’s corps finally arrived, so that about 40,000 French were now fighting 46,000 Russians."

citations.quote: Um 10 Uhr langte endlich die Division Verdier des Lannesschen Korps an, so daß nunmehr etwa 40,000 Franzosen gegen 46,000 Russen fochten.

claims.value: Höpfner infers that Napoleon ought to have had about 85,000 men with all troops directed on Friedland after detachments.
claims.rationale: Author’s reconstruction, not an actual simultaneous engaged return; source dependency on French campaign material remains possible. English rendering (ours): "although with all troops directed on Friedland, after deducting the various detachments, he must have been about 85,000 strong"

citations.quote: obgleich er mit den sämmtlichen auf Friedland dirigirten Truppen, nach Abzug der verschiedenen Detaschements, etwa 85,000 Mann stark sein mußte

claims.value: The printed order gives Ney movement initiative subject to Napoleon’s order to begin, while Napoleon places himself with the reserve.
claims.rationale: Order 12756 begins on p 334. The edition credits Thibaudeau and Mathieu Dumas on p 335; this is a historical printed transmission, not an inspected autograph or independent corroboration of Höpfner’s translation. English rendering (ours): "I shall be with the reserve." English rendering (ours): "One must always advance by the right and leave the movement initiative to Marshal Ney, who will await my orders to begin." English rendering of heading (ours): "Order 12756, at the bivouac behind Posthenen, 14 June 1807."

citations.quote: Je me trouverai à la réserve.
On doit toujours avancer par la droite, et on doit laisser l’initiative du mouvement au maréchal Ney, qui attendra mes ordres pour commencer.

12756. — ORDRES.
Au bivouac en arrière de Posthenen, 14 juin 1807.

claims.value: Höpfner attributes the retreat order to Bennigsen after observers on Friedland’s tower reported the whole French army approaching, at about 5 p. m.
claims.rationale: The preceding paragraph names Bennigsen and reports his memoir account; exact execution and subordinate authority remain unresolved. English rendering (ours): "He now immediately ordered the retreat" English rendering (ours): "Bennigsen had eagerly wished for darkness and was told at about five o’clock by officers he had posted to observe from Friedland’s tower that the whole French army was approaching. He immediately ordered the retreat."

citations.quote: Er befahl nun sogleich den Rückzug

Der General Bennigsen hatte sehnlichst die Dunkelheit herbeigewünscht, und wurde gegen 5 Uhr von einigen Offizieren, die er auf dem Thurm von Friedland zum Beobachten aufgestellt hatte, benachrichtigt, daß die ganze französische Armee im Anmarsch sei. Er befahl nun sogleich den Rückzug
